p.i: Deus Verbum ipse ex proprio lumine super-naturalis, beatæque suæ naturæ emittit naturaliter secundum propriam existentiam Spiritum sanctum. Nanque haud fieri potest, vt aliquid ex lumine alicuius appareat, & non naturaliter, & indiuise, & inexhauste inde effundatur, & tanquam illi coëxistens, & coœuum, & vti verus homo hic idem diuinam præeminentiam huius sancti Spiritus viua voce multimode reuelauit suis discipulis, sed non seruili modo, vti quicunque ex nostris sanctus, quod non purus homo erat ipse, sed Deus Verbum incarnatum diuino quodam modo, vti ex proprio lumine superdiuinæ suæ Deitatis effundens illum, vt ex fonte, promens nempe illum naturaliter. quæ duo vox φαίνω significat, φαίνω siquidem eluceo notat, & reuelo. Quapropter & Theologus Gregorius Oratione de Spiritu, Idem Spiritus, ait, ad Apostolos, ad Discipulos quoq; sigillatim se confert ad excipientium videlicet captum, modulumque sese impertiens, nimirum in Euangelij principio virtutes perficiens, post Christi passionem infusflatus, post ascensum in igneis linguis apparens, quod idem est atque a Saluatore promittitur, sed paulatim recipientium facultati commensuratus. Quin etiam ab ipso Iefu paulatim declaratur, vt ipse quoq; coperiens, Quod in Christi Discipulis ijsque [?] triфariam, prout ipsorum captus ferebat,

page.notes: Printed text is set in italic throughout; the Greek words φαίνω are in Greek letters as printed. The line ending "præeminentiam" carries a dash-like stroke, not a printed hyphen, so the word is written whole. "ijsque" is a doubtful reading ([?]). The line "triфariam" is a misreading of the Greek letter in the scan: the printed word is "trifariam", and the Greek phi was copied in error, so treat the word as "trifariam". Catchword "tri-" is the start of the next page's word. Page has no running head.
